title: Surface-Water-Controlled Drainage Composition Readiness Contract
purpose: Reconstruct and qualify the ownership boundaries needed for SWDRA=2 surface-water-controlled drainage without migrating the legacy surfacewater/MOD_drainage namespace as one object.

immutable_parameters: management thresholds, capacities and rule parameters
persistent_state_only_if_required_for_co: control memory only when exact legacy management semantics require history
dynamic_forcing_and_external_controls: prescribed primary or secondary water levels

provisional_decomposition_to_verify_agai.role: compute signed soil-to-surface-water exchange from explicit hydraulic summaries, immutable channel parameters and resolved control head
own the minimum committed storage/control memory needed to continue secondary surface-water dynamics

provisional_decomposition_to_verify_agai.ownership: physical control component, separate from numerical solver policy
provisional_decomposition_to_verify_agai.stateful: only where source semantics require history
provisional_decomposition_to_verify_agai.role: resolve target/control levels, supply/discharge actions and event boundaries
order checkpoint -> trial/retry -> commit/rollback, compose drainage exchange with storage/control, subdivide at physical events and publish accepted mass ledger

readiness_exit_before_any_production_can: reconstruct exact SurfaceWater task ordering and WLEVBAL semantics from frozen source
classify every legacy variable as immutable parameter, committed state, forcing/control, result or scratch
prove which water-level quantities are derivable from storage and which require persistent memory
map all supply/discharge/runoff/drainage terms into one signed mass convention
identify exact physical event boundaries without assuming daily execution
define rollback-safe runtime ordering with drainage exchange and soil-water trial state
split subsequent implementation children so exchange physics, stateful storage/control and runtime composition can be qualified independently
audit the resulting decomposition against all 30 SWAP architecture invariants
